Hi Elaine — thanks for the FYI and the forecast. High level, there are three pragmatic paths we typically offer for surges like this (summary below), plus a recommended play depending on how confident your forecast is. I attached a short options deck.

1) Temporary burst (fastest) — pay-as-you-go overage
   - Immediate capacity available; billed at standard consumption rates.
   - Discount: 0–6% off token rates depending on volume band.
   - No contract change; clean stop when surge ends.

2) Staged committed uplift (smoothing + discount) — recommended if you expect >3 months
   - Commit to an uplift amount annuitized over 12 months; we invoice monthly with a true-up.
   - Discount: typically 10–15% on uplift depending on sizing and term.
   - Co-term: can align uplift to your renewal date; small amendment fee may apply if shortening the term.

3) Blended annualize + voucher (billing-friendly)
   - We convert X% of surge to a voucher applied over remaining contract period and keep remainder pay-as-you-go.
   - Useful when procurement needs monthly line items but you don’t yet want a full commit.

Quick recommendation: if your Oct–Dec is real (your forecast looks like it), go staged committed uplift with monthly invoicing and a 12-month annualization. That gets you predictable unit economics and the biggest discount while avoiding one large invoice.

Questions for procurement to decide:
- Exact uplift quantity to commit (tokens / seats / capacity metric).
- Preferred payment terms (Net 30 / Net 60).
- Whether legal is comfortable with a small co-term amendment.

I put preliminary numbers in the attached options deck (redwood_mup_options.pdf). If you’re free Wed 16 10am PT or Thu 17 11am PT, I can walk through details and a pricing table for procurement.

Ben / Priyom — looped you both in. BrightSynth is looking at a 30–40% spike starting Oct 1 and prefers monthly smoothing vs a single prorated invoice. Procurement wants language we can hand them today.

My suggested commercial levers:
- Offer staged committed uplift annuitized over 12 months with a 12% discount on the uplift tranche (they get predictability; we keep ARR).
- Invoice monthly with a true-up so procurement has monthly line items.
- Provide a 15% buffer for the first 90 days (no charge up to buffer) to avoid immediate overages; buffer resets after 90 days.
- Payment terms: propose Net 60 (we can compromise to Net 30 if sales needs to close) — confirm cash impact.
- Co-term: waive amendment fee if they sign the uplift within 30 days, otherwise apply standard amendment admin fee.

Margin and legal notes for Priyom: staged uplift at 12% discount still maintains acceptable unit economics if we require annualization. If they insist on pay-as-you-go, cap discount at 6% and disallow voucher conversion.

Ben — can you own the procurement call? Priyom — please prepare a short co-term amendment (two-paragraph change) we can attach to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Sofia
